rounds.text: The valuation is difficult to support given that DB (International) Stock Brokers Ltd trades at a P/E of 38.8x [E1], which is higher than the sector benchmark of 33.19x [E6], while price growth has recently exceeded profit growth by 69% [E57]. Growth metrics reveal a sharp deceleration, evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth of 17% [E14] collapsing into a 3-year compounded sales growth of -2% [E16] and a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of -14% [E17]. Profitability remains modest and deteriorating, with a median return on equity of 7% over 10 years [E26] dropping to 4% over the last year [E29], accompanied by a low return on equity of 8.77% over the last 3 years [E63]. Furthermore, shareholders receive no cash return on their investment as the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4]. Conceded: the company maintains a price-to-book ratio of 1.52x [E2] compared to a much higher sector benchmark of 3.77x [E7], alongside an ROA of 2.68% [E8] and an ROCE of 7.15% [E10] that both outperform their respective sector benchmarks [E8, E10].

Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 38.8x [E1] against a sector benchmark of 33.19x [E6], and the trailing twelve-month sales growth has slowed to -14% [E17]. However, the bear ignores the compelling asset-level discount where the price-to-book ratio is just 1.5x compared to a vastly higher sector benchmark of 3.77x [E7]. This conservative valuation fails to reflect superior operational efficiency, proven by an ROA of 2.68% that comfortably outstrips the sector benchmark of -0.62% [E8]. Furthermore, the company delivers a strong ROCE of 7.15% that beats the sector benchmark of 4.41% [E10] as well as the sector median ROCE of 6.2% [E77]. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4], but recent fundamental screens explicitly highlight a robust operational rebound with sales up 48% year-over-year alongside strong overall sales growth [E66, E67].

Conceded: the company trades at a price-to-book ratio of 1.5x against a sector benchmark of 3.77x [E7]. However, the bull's reliance on this asset-level discount ignores the fact that this capital generates a weak return, with a median return on equity of just 4% over the last year [E29] and a low ROE of 8.77% over the last 3 years [E63]. Furthermore, while the bull highlights a strong ROA of 2.68% [E8] and an ROCE of 7.15% [E10], the company's fundamental delivery is deteriorating rapidly, evidenced by compounded sales growth collapsing to -2% over 3 years [E16] and contracting by -14% over the trailing twelve months [E17].
